metadata.title: Attention Is All You Need (Vaswani et al., 2017)
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of arXiv:1706.03762.

nodes.name: Scaled dot-product attention
nodes.statement: Given queries $Q \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times d_k}$, keys $K \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times d_k}$, and values $V \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times d_v}$: $\mathrm{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \mathrm{softmax}\left(\frac{QK^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right) V$. The scaling by $1/\sqrt{d_k}$ prevents softmax saturation for large $d_k$.

nodes.name: Multi-head attention
nodes.statement: Project $Q, K, V$ with $h$ different learned linear projections: $\mathrm{head}_i = \mathrm{Attention}(QW_i^Q, KW_i^K, VW_i^V)$ where $W_i^Q \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_k}$, $W_i^K \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_k}$, $W_i^V \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_v}$. Concatenate and project: $\mathrm{MultiHead}(Q,K,V) = \mathrm{Concat}(\mathrm{head}_1, \ldots, \mathrm{head}_h) W^O$.

nodes.name: Self-attention
nodes.statement: When $Q = K = V$ come from the same sequence (or its projection), the attention is called self-attention. Each position attends to all other positions in the same sequence. In the encoder, self-attention is over the full source sequence. In the decoder, self-attention is masked (causal) so position $i$ can only attend to positions $\le i$.

nodes.name: Cross-attention (encoder-decoder attention)
nodes.statement: In each decoder layer, a cross-attention sub-layer has $Q$ from the decoder and $K, V$ from the encoder output. This allows every decoder position to attend over all encoder positions, analogous to the attention mechanism in Bahdanau et al. (2014).

nodes.name: Position-wise feed-forward network
nodes.statement: Each layer contains a position-wise FFN applied identically to each position: $\mathrm{FFN}(x) = \max(0, xW_1 + b_1)W_2 + b_2$ (two linear layers with ReLU). The inner dimension is $d_{ff} = 2048$; the model dimension is $d_{\text{model}} = 512$.

nodes.name: Positional encoding
nodes.statement: Since the Transformer has no recurrence or convolution, positional information is injected via additive positional encodings. Sinusoidal encoding: $PE_{(pos, 2i)} = \sin(pos / 10000^{2i/d_{\text{model}}})$, $PE_{(pos, 2i+1)} = \cos(pos / 10000^{2i/d_{\text{model}}})$. These are added to the input embeddings.

nodes.name: Transformer encoder-decoder architecture
nodes.statement: The Transformer consists of an encoder stack of $N=6$ identical layers (each: multi-head self-attention + FFN, with residual connections and layer normalization) and a decoder stack of $N=6$ identical layers (each: masked multi-head self-attention + cross-attention + FFN, with residual connections and layer normalization). No recurrence.

nodes.name: Residual connections and layer normalization
nodes.statement: Each sub-layer (attention or FFN) is wrapped with a residual connection and layer normalization: $\mathrm{LayerNorm}(x + \mathrm{Sublayer}(x))$. This is the Pre-LN or Post-LN pattern (original uses Post-LN).

nodes.name: Computational advantages of self-attention over recurrence
nodes.statement: Self-attention has $O(1)$ sequential operations (fully parallelizable) vs $O(n)$ for RNNs. Maximum path length between any two positions is $O(1)$ for self-attention vs $O(n)$ for RNNs, enabling better gradient flow for long-range dependencies. Computational cost per layer is $O(n^2 d)$ for self-attention vs $O(n d^2)$ for RNNs, which is lower when $n < d$ (typical for NLP).

nodes.name: WMT 2014 translation results
nodes.statement: The Transformer achieves 28.4 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-German (new SOTA, +2 BLEU over previous best) and 41.8 BLEU on English-to-French (new SOTA), while training in 3.5 days on 8 GPUs. Significantly faster training than RNN-based models.
